questions.question: 🦅 Sami receives a patient with a malocclusion. He says: 'It's an Angle Class II, we need to act fast!' 🐆 Mina asks him: 'Are you sure about your classification?' What is Angle's classification?
options: A classification based on the relationship of the first permanent molars
A classification based on the patient's age
A classification based on the shape of the dental arch
A classification based on the color of the teeth
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains proudly: 'Angle's classification is based on the mesio-distal relationship of the first permanent molars. Class I = normal, Class II = distocclusion, Class III = mesiocclusion.' 🐆 Mina, a little annoyed: 'Well, for once you're right about the theory...'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina examines an 8-year-old child with mandibular retrognathia. 🦅 Sami tells her: 'Let's wait until growth is complete, it's simpler!' Mina replies: 'Not at all!' Why should it be treated early?
options: To take advantage of the growth spurt and stimulate the mandible
To prevent the child from growing too much
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Early treatment of Class II with an activator or bionator takes advantage of the growth spurt to stimulate the mandible.' 🦅 Sami admits: 'Fine, you're right. But I'm faster!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a panoramic radiograph, says: 'No need for cephalometry, I can see everything here!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'You can't see skeletal relationships!' What does cephalometry measure?
options: Skeletal and dental relationships in 2 dimensions
Only the position of the molars
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Cephalometry analyzes skeletal relationships (SNA, SNB, ANB) and dental inclinations.' 🐆 Mina, surprised: 'Well, for once you know your cephalometry! I'm impressed!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina examines a patient with severe crowding. 🦅 Sami proposes: 'Let's extract 4 premolars, it's fixed in 2 months!' Mina replies: 'Not so fast!' What needs to be analyzed first?
options: Crowding using the Bolton method and the curve of Spee
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Bolton analysis calculates crowding and guides towards extraction, expansion, or stripping.' 🦅 Sami grumbles: 'Yes, but you spend 3 hours calculating!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami wants to place brackets without a panoramic X-ray. 🐆 Mina opposes: 'That's dangerous!' Why is the panoramic X-ray mandatory?
options: To detect agenesis, impactions, cysts, and tumors
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The panoramic X-ray is the minimum radiological assessment to evaluate tooth germs, pathologies, and impactions.' 🐆 Mina, surprised: 'You're right Sami, it's the first time I've seen you so cautious!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, analyzing a lateral cephalogram, says: 'The ANB angle is 5°.' 🦅 Sami asks: 'What is the normal value?'
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The normal ANB angle is between 2 and 4°. Above = Class II, below = Class III.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll remember that, so I can shine in consultations!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a deep curve of Spee, says: 'It's not serious, we'll deal with it later.' 🐆 Mina corrects him: 'Yes, it is important!' Why?
options: A deep curve of Spee indicates a Class II and requires leveling
It doesn't change anything in the treatment
It's a sign of old age
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The curve of Spee is an essential parameter. A deep curve > 2 mm is often associated with a Class II.' 🐆 Mina, admiring: 'Bravo Sami, you're making progress!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina examines a 7-year-old child with an anterior open bite and thumb sucking. 🦅 Sami says: 'Let's wait until he grows up!' Mina replies: 'No, we need to act!' Why?
options: To prevent a definitive skeletal open bite
So the child stops sucking their thumb at 18
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Early interception of parafunctions before 8-9 years prevents skeletal open bites.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll prescribe a thumb-sucking device... but quickly!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing an impacted canine, proposes: 'Let's extract it right away!' 🐆 Mina tells him: 'Hold on!' What must be evaluated first?
options: The Nolla space to know the stage of development
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The Nolla space evaluates the stage of development of the canine. A conservative approach (space creation, traction) is preferable.' 🐆 Mina, impressed: 'Sami, you're becoming reasonable!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing an anterior crossbite, proposes: 'Maxillary expansion.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, extractions!' Who is right?
options: Mina, maxillary expansion is the first-line treatment
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Anterior crossbite is treated by maxillary expansion (quad-helix) or incisor repositioning.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, OK, but you spend 6 months doing the expansion!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami wants to use mini-screws for absolute anchorage. 🐆 Mina asks him: 'Have you analyzed the placement site?' Why is this important?
options: To evaluate bone density and root proximity
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Mini-screws require precise analysis of the placement site to avoid risks.' 🐆 Mina, astonished: 'Sami, have you become an expert in mini-screws? I'm blown away!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a severe Class III, says: 'We need a cephalometric assessment.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Useless, I can see the profile!' Who is right?
options: Mina, the cephalometric assessment is essential to quantify the discrepancy
Sami, the clinical profile is sufficient
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Cephalometry quantifies skeletal discrepancies and guides the decision between orthodontic treatment and surgery.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll do it... but it's long!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing atypical swallowing, says: 'It's not an orthodontic problem.' 🐆 Mina corrects him: 'Yes, absolutely!' Why?
options: Atypical swallowing is a major etiological factor in orthodontics
It has no impact on occlusion
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Myofunctional disorders influence occlusion and treatment stability.' 🐆 Mina, surprised: 'Sami, you're impressing me, you know your subject!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina explains to a 50-year-old patient that orthodontic treatment is possible. 🦅 Sami says: 'At 50, it's too late!' Who is right?
options: Mina, adult orthodontics is perfectly feasible
Sami, it's too late to move teeth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Adult orthodontics is possible with adapted forces and aligners.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, OK, but I would have done surgery!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami wants to place brackets without checking the patient's hygiene. 🐆 Mina opposes: 'That's a mistake!' Why?
options: Poor hygiene with brackets can cause decalcifications and cavities
Hygiene is not important in orthodontics
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Evaluation and motivation in hygiene are essential before any orthodontic treatment.' 🐆 Mina, admiring: 'Sami, you're starting to think like me!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, analyzing the end of growth, says: 'The spheno-occipital synchondrosis is closed.' 🦅 Sami asks: 'Why is that important?'
options: It indicates the end of growth and the cessation of orthopedic treatments
It indicates the start of treatment
It indicates that extraction is needed
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The closure of the spheno-occipital synchondrosis marks the end of growth. Orthopedic treatments must be stopped.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll look... but quickly!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a Nolla space stage 5, says: 'We can extract the canine!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not so fast!' What does this stage mean?
options: The canine is erupting, space needs to be created
The canine is impacted and must be extracted
The canine is in a good position
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Nolla stage 5 means that the canine is erupting. Traction or space creation is indicated.' 🐆 Mina, astonished: 'Sami, you're becoming a real specialist!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with 8 mm of crowding, proposes: 'Expansion + stripping.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, extractions!' What does the Bolton method say?
options: The Bolton method calculates crowding to guide the decision
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The Bolton method quantifies crowding. Crowding > 6 mm may justify extractions.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, OK, I'll calculate... but quickly!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a curve of Spee at 3 mm, says: 'It's not serious.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Yes, it is significant!' What needs to be done?
options: Leveling of the occlusal plane with continuous arches
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'A curve of Spee > 2 mm requires leveling to obtain a horizontal occlusal plane.' 🐆 Mina, impressed: 'Sami, you're on fire today!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a Class II division 1, says: 'We need an activator.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, brackets!' Who is right for a 10-year-old child?
options: Mina, functional appliances are indicated in growing children
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Functional appliances (activator, bionator) harness growth in children.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, OK, but I'm faster with brackets!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with an 8 mm overjet, says: 'Let's extract the upper premolars!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not so fast!' What needs to be evaluated?
options: The skeletal component and residual growth
Only the color of the teeth
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'A significant overjet can be of skeletal or dental origin. A cephalometric assessment is essential.' 🐆 Mina, admiring: 'Sami, you're a real professional!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, analyzing a patient with facial asymmetry, proposes: 'A complete assessment.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Useless, I can clearly see the asymmetry!' Why is the assessment important?
options: To quantify the asymmetry and plan orthodontic or surgical treatment
Asymmetry can be seen clinically, it's sufficient
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Facial asymmetry requires cephalometric analysis and functional evaluation.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll do it... but it's long!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing an anterior open bite in an adult, says: 'It's too late to treat.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not at all!' What does she propose?
options: An orthodontic approach with mini-screws or orthognathic surgery
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Anterior open bite in adults can be treated by orthodontics (with mini-screws) or orthognathic surgery.' 🐆 Mina, surprised: 'Sami, you're really surprising today!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing gingival recession in an orthodontic patient, says: 'We need to stop the forces.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, we continue!' Who is right?
options: Mina, excessive forces can worsen recessions
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Orthodontic forces must be adapted to avoid gingival recessions.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll reduce the forces... but it's longer!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami and 🐆 Mina discuss retention after treatment. Sami says: 'We remove the brackets and that's it!' Mina replies: 'Not at all!' Why is retention crucial?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Retention is the key to stability in orthodontics. The risks of relapse are high without retention.' 🐆 Mina, astonished: 'Sami, when you want to, you're a real expert!'
